::: {.home-hero}
# George G. Vega Yon, Ph.D.

[Associate Research Professor · Division of Epidemiology, University of Utah]{.home-hero-role}
:::

::: {.home-lead}

I am an Associate Research Professor at the
<a href="https://medicine.utah.edu/internalmedicine/epidemiology/" target="_blank">Division of Epidemiology at the University of Utah</a>, with adjunct appointments in the departments of Population Health Sciences and the Kahlert School of Computing.

My research builds statistical methods and open-source software for networks and other <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Complex_system&oldid=1369270950" target="_blank">complex systems</a>: exponential random graph models (ERGMs) for the small networks that field studies actually collect, agent-based models of epidemic spread and behavioral diffusion, and the high-performance <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Computational_statistics&oldid=1340808080" target="_blank">statistical computing</a> that makes both tractable. The work runs from method to software to application — [`ergmito`, `epiworld`, and `rgexf`](software.qmd) on one side; [measles outbreak modeling, weapon-use transmission in officer networks, and PrEP adoption across physician networks](research.qmd) on the other. Over the last few years I have folded LLM and agentic AI tooling into that pipeline.

My training is in Public Policy (M.A. <a href="https://www.uai.cl/" target="_blank">UAI</a>, 2011), Economics (M.Sc. <a href="https://caltech.edu" target="_blank">Caltech</a>, 2015), and Biostatistics (Ph.D. <a href="https://usc.edu" target="_blank">USC</a>, 2020).

I obtained my Ph.D. in Biostatistics under the supervision of <a href="https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=Zj5ky5gAAAAJ&hl=en" target="_blank">Prof. Paul Marjoram</a> and <a href="https://kayladelahaye.net" target="_blank">Prof. Kayla de la Haye</a>, with my dissertation titled "<a href="thesis.pdf" target="_blank">Essays on Bioinformatics and Social Network Analysis: Statistical and Computational Methods for Complex Systems</a>."
:::
